questions.prompt: What does your company do?
questions.why: Check whether a reader understands the user and function quickly.
questions.answerFrame: We are building [function] for [specific user] so they can [concrete job].
questions.followup: What can I run today?

questions.prompt: Who needs this right now?
questions.why: Test urgency beyond general enthusiasm about physical AI.
questions.answerFrame: [Role] doing [task] recently encountered [specific failure] and currently uses [workaround].
questions.followup: Who would pay and why this month?

questions.prompt: Why can't they use existing solutions?
questions.why: Find a precise unmet need and a fair comparison.
questions.answerFrame: [Tool] handles [capability], but for [specific condition] the user still does [costly work]; we are testing [improvement].
questions.followup: Have you reproduced that limit yourself?

questions.prompt: What is your non-obvious insight?
questions.why: Separate a testable mechanism from generic self-praise.
questions.answerFrame: We observed [pattern]. We think [mechanism] explains it, and [test] will distinguish it from [alternative].
questions.followup: What would prove this wrong?

questions.prompt: Why is now the right time?
questions.why: Connect recent enabling changes to an actual buying trigger.
questions.answerFrame: [Change] enables [new workflow]; [customer event] makes [problem] urgent. The demand assumption remains [status].
questions.followup: Why was this not viable two years ago?

questions.prompt: What is the first narrow product?
questions.why: Check whether the scope can ship and be evaluated.
questions.answerFrame: Our first scope is [sensor and contact experiment] delivering [measurable output] to [user].
questions.followup: What did you deliberately postpone?

questions.prompt: Is this a physics engine, a renderer or a world model?
questions.why: Prevent conflating observations, physical transitions and planning.
questions.answerFrame: Today [artifact] predicts [output] from [inputs]. [Dynamics/control layers] are [implemented/planned], so our present claim is [narrow scope].
questions.followup: Where does action-conditioned state evolution occur?

questions.prompt: What would make the PoC successful?
questions.why: Define a falsifiable result before cherry-picking a clip.
questions.answerFrame: We will call this useful if [metric] improves over [baseline] on [reserved conditions] under [budget].
questions.followup: What result would make you change direction?

questions.prompt: How far along are you?
questions.why: Require dated work rather than a roadmap alone.
questions.answerFrame: We have [verified artifact] as of [date], demonstrating [exact capability]. [Next capability] remains unfinished.
questions.followup: Show the strongest result and its failure case.

questions.prompt: How long have you worked on this full-time?
questions.why: Understand velocity and actual commitment.
questions.answerFrame: [Founder] has worked [status] since [date]; during that period we shipped [specific artifacts].
questions.followup: What changes if accepted?

questions.prompt: What changed in the last 30 days?
questions.why: Measure execution with a real before/after.
questions.answerFrame: On [earlier date] we could [old state]; today [artifact] can [new state], with [evidence].
questions.followup: Which change mattered most to a user?

questions.prompt: What will you build next?
questions.why: Check dependency awareness and speed to evidence.
questions.answerFrame: Next we will [bounded experiment] to resolve [uncertainty]; [owner] needs [dependency] and will report [artifact].
questions.followup: What can proceed if that dependency slips?

questions.prompt: What metrics matter before launch?
questions.why: Avoid adopting irrelevant DAU or vanity figures.
questions.answerFrame: We track [physical error and benchmark] plus [qualified evaluations/repeat usage]. Current values are [verified or unknown].
questions.followup: Which metric predicts willingness to pay?

questions.prompt: How many users, pilots and customers do you have?
questions.why: Distinguish stages of evidence.
questions.answerFrame: We have [actual number/status] at [defined stage]. [Interviews] are not counted as pilots or revenue.
questions.followup: How many ran it without your help?

questions.prompt: Do users come back?
questions.why: Test repeated workflow value rather than demo interest.
questions.answerFrame: [Defined cohort] repeated [useful action] over [period]; if not yet measured, state that and the plan.
questions.followup: What would cause them to stop using it?

questions.prompt: What is slowing you down?
questions.why: Identify the real technical or operational constraint.
questions.answerFrame: Our current bottleneck is [specific issue], evidenced by [trace]. We are testing [smallest intervention].
questions.followup: Why not choose an easier first task?

questions.prompt: What did not work?
questions.why: Look for learning and scientific candor.
questions.answerFrame: [Approach] failed on [condition]. We learned [supported finding] and changed [specific next step].
questions.followup: How did you rule out an implementation bug?

questions.prompt: Who are your direct and indirect competitors?
questions.why: Test market awareness across research and practical alternatives.
questions.answerFrame: Direct alternatives include [tactile tools]; broader substitutes are [real data/internal work/platforms]. Our proposed advantage is [measured or unproven].
questions.followup: Which alternative wins today?

questions.prompt: Why won't NVIDIA build this into Isaac?
questions.why: Test complement strategy and defensibility under platform improvement.
questions.answerFrame: They already support [verified capability]. We are testing value in [specific calibration/data/validation workflow], measured by [outcome], while integrating with [platform/status].
questions.followup: If their rendering improves tomorrow, why do users keep you?

questions.prompt: Why would someone pay instead of using open source?
questions.why: Find a purchase reason beyond code availability.
questions.answerFrame: The payment hypothesis is [saved work/reliable validation/support], not mere access to code. We will test it with [scoped paid evaluation].
questions.followup: What part could a capable engineer rebuild in a week?

questions.prompt: How big can the market become?
questions.why: Require a defensible path from initial segment to expansion.
questions.answerFrame: Our initial estimate is [qualifying organizations] times [validated contract value]. Expansion into [workflow] depends on [unproven evidence].
questions.followup: What supports each multiplier?

questions.prompt: Who writes the check?
questions.why: Separate enthusiastic user from budget holder.
questions.answerFrame: [Engineer] uses it; [manager/lab lead] controls [budget]. Our evidence is [conversation/accepted evaluation], or this is still unknown.
questions.followup: How long does approval take?

questions.prompt: What will you charge?
questions.why: Test value capture and awareness of uncertainty.
questions.answerFrame: Our initial pricing hypothesis is [fixed-fee pilot/team license]. [Price] is [proposed/accepted/unknown], based on [value and costs].
questions.followup: What have users actually agreed to pay?

questions.prompt: How will you get your first customers?
questions.why: Check a concrete repeatable acquisition experiment.
questions.answerFrame: We will start with [narrow segment] through [credible access], run [task-specific evaluations] and track [conversion to paid/repeated use].
questions.followup: How does this scale beyond your own contacts?

questions.prompt: What are the delivery costs?
questions.why: Reveal services burden and compute/support economics.
questions.answerFrame: Each [pilot/license] currently requires [measured costs or unknown]. We expect [repeatable step] to reduce [cost], which remains to be tested.
questions.followup: How much founder labor is hidden in the margin?

questions.prompt: What becomes hard to copy?
questions.why: Distinguish an aspiration from an accumulated asset.
questions.answerFrame: Potential durable assets are [specific data/protocol/integration], but today we have [actual asset]. We will test whether it improves [customer outcome].
questions.followup: Why does more data improve the product rather than just its size?

questions.prompt: Why is this a company rather than only a research project?
questions.why: Check demand and repeatable value.
questions.answerFrame: The research question is [hypothesis]. The company hypothesis is that [buyer] repeatedly pays for [job], and we have [current evidence/gap].
questions.followup: What evidence would make you abandon the business idea?

questions.prompt: Who are the founders and what does each person do?
questions.why: Make individual ability and responsibility inspectable.
questions.answerFrame: [Name] built [specific work]; [name] owns [specific work]. Unknown roles must be completed before submission.
questions.followup: Who can debug the measurement and mechanics pipeline?

questions.prompt: How do the founders know each other?
questions.why: Understand relationship depth through actual shared work.
questions.answerFrame: We met [when/how] and have worked together on [specific artifacts] since [date].
questions.followup: What have you shipped together under pressure?

questions.prompt: How is equity split?
questions.why: Check clarity, alignment and future commitment.
questions.answerFrame: The current split is [actual percentages] with [documented terms/status], reflecting [honest rationale].
questions.followup: Are all founders satisfied and committed?

questions.prompt: Who is building the core technology?
questions.why: Confirm capability resides with the founding team.
questions.answerFrame: [Founder] implements [core parts], with [licensed tools/collaborators] used for [specific scope].
questions.followup: What work depends on a university or external contractor?

questions.prompt: What is the hardest challenge you faced together?
questions.why: Assess how collaboration works in practice.
questions.answerFrame: During [event], [problem] occurred. [People] did [specific actions], producing [supported outcome].
questions.followup: What disagreement did you resolve and how?

questions.prompt: Can the team work on this full-time?
questions.why: Expose actual time and location constraints.
questions.answerFrame: Today [actual status]. If [condition], [founders] can transition by [date]; [constraint] remains unresolved.
questions.followup: What happens if funding takes longer?

questions.prompt: Why are you the team to build it?
questions.why: Tie capability to inspectable contributions, not status claims.
questions.answerFrame: We have directly built [specific work] and learned [domain insight]. We still need [gap] and will address it through [plan].
questions.followup: What is your largest capability gap?

questions.prompt: What are your burn and runway?
questions.why: Check operational awareness without false precision.
questions.answerFrame: We have [cash] as of [date] and expect [net burn] under [assumptions], giving [runway]. Unknown values must be completed.
questions.followup: How does hardware spending change the plan?

questions.prompt: What real data did you use?
questions.why: Avoid ambiguous synthetic-only claims.
questions.answerFrame: Real data calibrates [parameters]; synthetic data trains [model]; reserved real data evaluates [metric]. [Any real fine-tuning] is [disclosed status].
questions.followup: Did the evaluation influence model selection?

questions.prompt: How do you know the mechanics are correct?
questions.why: Separate image matching from physical fidelity.
questions.answerFrame: We measure [physical quantity] independently and compare [prediction] on [held-out motion]; images are evaluated separately.
questions.followup: Which contact mode currently fails?

questions.prompt: Can touch uniquely identify friction or stiffness?
questions.why: Test awareness of inverse-problem ambiguity.
questions.answerFrame: We infer [effective parameter] only under [controlled conditions]. Multiple parameters may explain the same signal; [extra probe/reference] helps distinguish them.
questions.followup: What happens with a different gel or object shape?

questions.prompt: Does your model capture shear and slip?
questions.why: Prevent normal indentation evidence being generalized to friction.
questions.answerFrame: We have validated [specific modes] and have not yet validated [others]. Shear requires [planned measurement/model].
questions.followup: How do you distinguish incipient slip from gross sliding?

questions.prompt: What does your FPS number include?
questions.why: Disambiguate rendering speed, full steps and batch throughput.
questions.answerFrame: At [settings], [timed pipeline] produces [throughput] with [single-scene latency] and [memory]. It excludes [explicit work].
questions.followup: How does accuracy change at that setting?

questions.prompt: What exactly transferred to real hardware?
questions.why: Separate perception from a learned control policy.
questions.answerFrame: [Estimator/policy] trained on [data] was frozen before [real evaluation]; [calibration] occurred beforehand. The claim is [perception/control/policy transfer].
questions.followup: How many attempts succeeded and which failed?

questions.prompt: What baseline could explain the result more simply?
questions.why: Ensure engine value is isolated rather than only tactile usefulness.
questions.answerFrame: We compare [our engine] with [appropriate baseline] under [matched settings]. Touch-versus-no-touch is a separate ablation.
questions.followup: Did all methods receive the same calibration budget?

questions.prompt: What is genuinely held out?
questions.why: Avoid random-frame leakage and overbroad transfer claims.
questions.answerFrame: We reserve [objects/trajectories/days] and select settings only on [development set]. This supports [bounded claim].
questions.followup: Could adjacent frames or shared specimens leak information?

questions.prompt: What does your existing vibration research establish?
questions.why: Preserve the scope of earlier evidence.
questions.answerFrame: It demonstrates [offline spectrum-prediction/development pipeline]. It does not establish force identification, forward dynamics or robot control; synthetic mechanics results remain synthetic.
questions.followup: How does that software accelerate the next physical experiment?

questions.prompt: When should users not trust the simulator?
questions.why: Check calibration limits and useful failure reporting.
questions.answerFrame: The validated envelope is [loads/speeds/geometries/sensor]. Outside it, [warning/measurement requirement] applies; [failure] is currently known.
questions.followup: How will a user notice they are outside that envelope?
